Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling (both under her own name and her pseudonym Robert Galbraith): | Title | Year | Notes | |-------|------|-------| | **Harry Potter series** | 1997‑2007 | 7‑book saga that made her an international icon.
• *Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s/ Sorcerer’s Stone* (1997)
• *Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets* (1998)
• *Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban* (1999)
• *Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire* (2000)
• *Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix* (2003)
• *Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince* (2005)
• *Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows* (2007) | | **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 | A companion book to the Harry Potter world, later adapted into a film series. | | **Quidditch Through the Ages** | 2001 | Another companion book detailing the history of Quidditch. | | **The Tales of Beedle the Bard** | 2008 | A collection of wizarding fairy tales. | | **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. | | **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel published under her own name. | | **The Cuckoo’s Calling** | 2013 | First book in the *Cormoran Strike* series, published under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith. | | **The Silkworm** | 2014 | Second book in the *Cormoran Strike* series. | | **Career of Evil** | 2015 | Third book in the *Cormoran Strike* series. | | **Lethal White** | 2018 | Fourth book in the *Cormoran Strike* series. | | **The Ink Black** | 2022 | Fifth book in the *Cormoran Strike* series. | These titles cover the breadth of Rowling’s work—from the beloved wizarding world to her ventures into adult crime fiction and children’s literature.
